_comment: Task 262 sub-task 1 — the relational query set.
Taxonomy from LoCoMo + LongMemEval (the shared question categories both
papers in the 2026-08-07 research break benchmark on): single-hop /
multi-hop / temporal / preference. Two of the four are CONTROLS by design:
single-hop  the answer is directly findable by flat search. Traversal must
not REGRESS it — a graph pipeline that pushes true answers out
of the top-5 with neighbours is a loss, not a win.
preference  the same control on the USER tier (LongMemEval's category).
temporal    reachable by walking `superseded_by`, which is NOT a `related:`
edge and therefore survives the unlinked twin unchanged. If the
canary margin shows up here too, the margin is measuring
traversal-in-general and not LINKING — that is the false-positive
this control exists to catch. Four questions, not two: a control
of size two moves in 0.5 steps and cannot resolve anything.
multi-hop   the measured type. `edge: related`.
`hops` is how many edges separate the query's best flat hit from the answer.
`reach` states honestly how findable the answer is WITHOUT any edge:
link-only  the answer body shares no distinctive term with the query
partial    the answer shares some query vocabulary, so flat can score > 0
A set of only `link-only` questions would make the canary margin a trivial
0 -> 1 step; the `partial` cases are what make it a graded measurement.
